question: What is the solid form of water called?
why: Water becomes ice when it freezes.

question: Which of these is a source of fresh water?
why: River water is not salty. Oceans, seas and salt lakes are salty.

question: Water vapour rises high up and cools. It then forms tiny drops that make ...
why: The drops gather in the sky as clouds.

question: Why does less rainwater soak into the ground in cities?
a: The soil in cities is too hot
c: Cement and concrete cover the ground and stop water soaking in
d: Rainwater is too heavy to soak in
why: Roads and floors are covered with cement. The water runs off instead of going into the ground.

question: Which order of steps in the water cycle is correct?
a: Rain falls, clouds form, the Sun heats water, vapour rises
b: The Sun heats water, vapour rises, vapour cools into clouds, rain falls
c: Vapour cools into clouds, the Sun heats water, rain falls, vapour rises
d: The Sun heats water, rain falls, vapour rises, clouds form
why: Heat makes vapour first. The vapour cools into clouds. Then rain falls.

question: A leaking tap wastes 4 litres of water every day. How much water is wasted in 30 days?
why: 4 x 30 = 120 litres. Fixing small leaks saves a lot of water.

question: A river starts in the hills. Where does it usually end?
why: Most rivers flow down and join the sea.

question: What is a dam built across a river used for?
why: A dam holds back water so it can be used later.

question: Which river flows through Maharashtra, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh?
why: The Godavari flows through these states and a few more.

question: Why do farmers near a river often grow more crops?
a: The soil near rivers is always dry
b: The river gives water to water their fields
d: Fields near rivers get no rain
why: River water can be used to irrigate fields.

question: A new dam floods a village. What is the best step?
a: Give the families new homes and land first
b: Close the dam and forget the village
c: Tell people to move without help
why: People who lose their homes need new homes and land that are safe.

question: Why do fish die when a factory lets dirty water into a river?
b: The fish get too much food
d: The water gets poisoned and has less oxygen
why: Dirty water has harmful stuff and uses up oxygen that fish need.

question: What are the tiny living things that spoil food called?
why: Microbes are too small to see. They grow in food and spoil it.

question: Which teeth at the front are used to cut food?
why: Incisors are sharp and flat. They cut food.

question: Which is an old way to keep food from spoiling?
a: Keeping it in a warm wet place
why: Dry food has no water. Microbes cannot grow without water.

question: Why does a layer of oil help keep pickle fresh?
a: The oil keeps air away from the pickle
d: The oil makes the jar warm
why: Microbes need air to grow. Oil blocks the air.

question: Which shows the way food moves in our body?
a: Mouth, stomach, food pipe, small intestine
b: Stomach, mouth, food pipe, small intestine
c: Mouth, small intestine, stomach, food pipe
d: Mouth, food pipe, stomach, small intestine
why: Food is chewed in the mouth. It then goes down the food pipe to the stomach and the small intestine.

question: A cut fruit goes bad faster than a whole fruit. Why?
c: The cut part lets microbes in easily
why: The skin protects the fruit. Cutting it opens a way for microbes.

question: Fruit peels go into which kind of waste bin?
why: Peels are food waste. That is wet waste.

question: A classmate falls and gets hurt. What should you do first?
why: A teacher can give help quickly.

question: Which of these is dry waste?
why: Paper is dry waste. The others are food waste.

question: Which colour of floor tile stays cooler in the hot Sun?
why: White reflects most of the Sun's heat. Dark colours take in more heat.

question: The fire alarm rings at school. What should you do?
c: Walk calmly to the assembly point
why: Stay calm, follow your teacher and go to the assembly point. Do not go back inside.

question: Why is collecting rainwater from the roof a good idea?
b: It saves water and helps fill the water under the ground
why: Stored rainwater can be used later. Rainwater that soaks in also refills groundwater.

question: On which date do we celebrate Republic Day?
why: Republic Day is on 26 January each year.

question: Which animal is India's national animal?
why: The tiger is India's national animal.

question: How many spokes does the Ashoka Chakra in our flag have?
why: The wheel in the middle of the flag has 24 spokes.

question: Why do we celebrate Republic Day on 26 January?
a: The first school opened that day
b: India won a cricket match that day
c: The Constitution came into effect on that day in 1950
d: The Taj Mahal was built that day
why: On 26 January 1950 India's Constitution began. That made India a republic.

question: Which sentence best explains 'unity in diversity'?
a: Everyone in India speaks the same language
b: People speak many languages and have many customs, yet live together as one country
why: India has many languages and customs, but its people share one country.

question: Which pair is matched correctly?
why: The banyan is India's national tree. The national flower is the lotus, the bird is the peacock and the fruit is the mango.

question: In which sea are the Andaman and Nicobar Islands?
why: These islands lie in the Bay of Bengal.

question: Which of these is a state in North-East India?
why: Assam is in the North-East. The others are not.

question: Which of these rivers starts in the Western Ghats?
why: The Kaveri starts in the Western Ghats. The others start elsewhere.

question: Where do mangrove trees grow?
b: In salty, muddy water where rivers meet the sea
why: Mangroves grow near the coast where river water meets sea water.

question: Some mangrove roots stick up out of the mud. Why?
a: They help the trees breathe in muddy soil
why: Mud has little air. The upward roots take in air for the tree.

question: A coastal village cuts down its mangrove forest. What is most likely to happen?
b: There is more shade on the beach
d: The coast faces more damage from storms and waves
why: Mangrove roots hold the soil and slow down waves and storms.

question: What gives our body the energy to play and study?
why: Food stores energy that our body uses.

question: Which of these needs petrol to run?
why: A scooter's engine burns petrol.

question: Which of these energy sources will not run out?
why: The Sun keeps shining. Coal, petrol and diesel can run out.

question: A battery in a torch stores energy. When we switch the torch on, what do we get?
why: The stored energy changes into light.

question: Why is solar energy better than coal for clean air?
a: Solar energy is made of coal
why: Burning coal makes smoke and harmful gases. Solar energy does not.

question: Which action saves energy?
a: Keep all lights on in the day
b: Leave the TV on while you sleep
c: Switch off the fan and light when you leave the room
why: Switching off what you are not using saves energy.

question: Cotton cloth comes from which source?
why: Cotton fibre grows in the fruit of the cotton plant.

question: Wool for sweaters mostly comes from which animal?
why: Sheep hair is cut, spun into yarn and used to make wool.

question: Silk threads come from the cocoon of which insect?
why: The silkworm spins a cocoon of silk thread.

question: What happens in weaving?
c: Threads are tied in one long knot
d: Threads cross over and under each other
why: In weaving, one set of threads goes over and under another set.

question: Which order shows the life cycle of the silk moth?
why: The moth lays eggs. A caterpillar hatches, spins a cocoon, and a moth comes out.

question: Why are cotton clothes comfortable in hot weather?
b: Cotton soaks up sweat and lets air pass
d: Cotton keeps all the air out
why: Cotton takes in sweat and lets air move, so we stay cooler.

question: What causes day and night?
a: The Sun goes round the Earth
b: The Earth spins on its axis
why: The Earth spins. The side facing the Sun has day and the other side has night.

question: In which season does most of India get heavy rain?
why: The monsoon brings heavy rain to most of India.

question: When it is day in India, it is night in which country?
why: The USA is on almost the opposite side of the Earth. Nepal, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh are close to India.

question: Which of these changes happens again and again every year?
why: Seasons come back in the same order each year. The others happen in a day.

question: Assam gets heavy monsoon rain and Rajasthan stays mostly dry. Why?
a: Assam is nearer to the Sun
b: Places in India have different climates and rainfall
d: The monsoon only visits Assam by chance
why: Climate and rainfall change from place to place in India.

question: Which of these changes takes the longest time?
a: A seed growing into a big tree
c: The sky turning orange at sunset
why: A tree takes many years. The others take minutes or hours.

question: The oceans of the Earth are ...
why: Water flows from one ocean to the next. They form one big ocean.

question: What does 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' mean?
d: The whole world is one family
why: It teaches us that all people and living things are like one family.

question: Which of these can cross country borders freely?
why: Clouds float across borders. The other things stay in one place.

question: Why do some birds, like the rosy starling, come to India in winter?
b: To find food and a warmer place
why: In their home it is too cold and food is hard to find, so they travel to warmer places.

question: Which sentence shows that nature has no boundaries?
a: A river can flow through many countries
c: Every country has its own sky
why: A river does not stop at borders.

question: Plastic thrown into a river in one town reaches the sea and harms animals far away. What does this show?
b: Rubbish stays where it is thrown
why: Rivers carry things to the sea. What we do in one place can affect others far away.
